Quantization reduces the precision of key-value cache representations by lowering the bit-width of stored values—from standard 16-bit floating-point (FP16) or 32-bit (FP32) to lower bit-widths such as INT8 or INT4.

The claim that "Google just figured out how to run LLMs on 6x less memory" (from [S1]) refers to **TurboQuant**, which compresses KV caches to **3 bits per value**—a 5.3× reduction from standard 16–32-bit representations.

The gap between standard inference (16–32 bits) and compressed representations (e.g., 3 bits) is where the bottleneck lies. Google's TurboQuant claims to close this gap without modifying the model, suggesting a novel algorithmic approach to quantization that may involve advanced error modeling or reconstruction during inference.
